clue.text: Style of service, nearly ready to fight

parts.note: just under a figure is nearly that figure
to arm is to make ready for battle

explanation.surface: A tennis server whose style is almost combative.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma breaks the definition off; 'nearly' and 'ready to fight' are two separate pieces read in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving with the hand below shoulder level is a recognised way of delivering a ball in tennis or cricket.

clue.text: Clever, taking top off table

indicators.note: removing the top of a word drops its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clever person clearing the top of a table.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone capable and skilled can be described as clever, a common synonym.

clue.text: Auntie's son keeps us in small change

indicators.note: one word placed inside another sits within it

parts.note: a coin is a piece of small change
taken as written

explanation.surface: A relative who keeps the family short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps' looks like the container signal but only links; the insertion is signalled by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The son of one's aunt is a first cousin, a family relationship.

clue.text: Coarser king not going to the bank

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written
a tier is a bank or row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A rough-mannered king who avoids the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money or a river, but here it is a raised row, as in banks of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood with more knots has a rougher, less fine grain, so knottier timber is coarser.

clue.text: Had winter fun and got bigger quickly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: threw balls of packed snow
second meaning: grew rapidly, like a rolling ball of snow

explanation.surface: Someone enjoyed a snowy day and grew fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both pelting people with packed snow and escalating rapidly, from a ball growing as it rolls.

clue.text: Relaxed, having a tea set with a bit missing

indicators.note: a bit missing means a word loses a letter, here its end

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written; its final letter goes

explanation.surface: Feeling easy with an incomplete tea service.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a chipped tea set; in fact 'set' simply drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand at ease is to be relaxed, an idiom from the military command.

clue.text: Eleven in succession?

parts.note: surface reading: a team or the number after ten
setter's reading: written as numerals, eleven is a one followed by another one

explanation.surface: A cricket eleven coming out to bat in order.
explanation.walkthrough: The figures 11 are literally one digit beside another.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means singly and in turn, each following the last.

clue.text: Eric keeps turning to aphrodisiac

indicators.note: turning a word round makes it read backwards
a word that keeps another holds it inside

parts.note: taken as written
the little word read backwards

explanation.surface: A man called Eric resorting to a love potion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aphrodisiac' is usually a noun, but it also works as an adjective meaning arousing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphrodisiac arouses sexual desire, so as an adjective it is close to sexually stimulating.

clue.text: A number I ensnare in New York

indicators.note: something placed in another word sits inside it

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
taken as written
to net is to catch or ensnare

explanation.surface: Someone trapping something in New York City.
explanation.walkthrough: I and NET together sit between the N and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a figure, nine tens, so it is an example of a number.

clue.text: Her early start is at this point

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A woman who starts early arriving at a particular moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb indicates this place or this stage, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Casual clothes will make a good loser curse

parts.note: a good sport takes defeat gracefully
to swear is to curse

explanation.surface: A bad loser's oath turned into an outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies a gracious loser would never curse; the two are simply joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing made for athletic activity is widely worn as informal everyday dress.

clue.text: Sponsor wants no part altered

indicators.note: altered letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A backer insists on no changes to any section.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron gives financial support to an artist or cause, much as a sponsor does.

clue.text: Colourful fish will not deceive Hercule Poirot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally a herring dyed by smoking
second meaning: a false clue planted to mislead, which the detective always sees through

explanation.surface: A fish that fails to fool Agatha Christie's detective.
explanation.walkthrough: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's Belgian sleuth, whom no false trail fools.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a smoked kipper, and figuratively a misleading lead in a mystery story.

clue.text: Looks like meat; is it stew?

indicators.note: a stew mixes its ingredients together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something resembles meat, so is it a stew?
explanation.definitionFit: To copy or resemble something is to look like it, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Mr North is suppressing an ode, not very old

indicators.note: pressing down on something holds it within

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A man called North censoring a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr North' reads as a person's name, but splits into a title and a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recent or current is the opposite of ancient, so it is up to date.

clue.text: "Need gear changing?" asks this deserter

indicators.note: changing the letters puts them in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A runaway asking whether the car's gears need shifting.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade abandons a cause or side, the same as a traitor or turncoat.

clue.text: By restraining thunder, it'll keep you dry

indicators.note: a word that restrains another holds it in

parts.note: taken as written
a roll of thunder is its rumble

explanation.surface: Holding back a thunderstorm keeps you from getting wet.
explanation.walkthrough: A brolly is British slang for an umbrella.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella shields you from rain, which is a cryptic description rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Fancy gaining at the end of the day

indicators.note: the end of a word is just its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of this word
earning is gaining money

explanation.surface: Imagining a profit at close of business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as a verb about imagining, but is the noun for desire.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a liking or longing, so yearning is a synonym for it as a noun.

clue.text: Secures one hundred lights

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
lamps are lights

explanation.surface: Someone fixing a hundred lamps in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To clamp something is to fasten or hold it firmly, so the verb matches.

clue.text: Alter man to become loving?

indicators.note: becoming something else means a change of form, so letters rearrange

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Can a man be changed to become more caring?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alter' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; the question mark flags that loving is only one sense of motherly.
explanation.definitionFit: Motherly feeling is typically warm and caring, so loving is an example of it.

clue.text: Accepts embraces

definitions.meaning: first meaning: takes on, as a child or an idea
second meaning: takes up a cause or belief

explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a plan or a child is to take it on as one's own, both accepting and embracing it.

clue.text: Aide-de-camp cuts up map, being reckless

indicators.note: a word that cuts another splits it open and sits in the gap

parts.note: taken as written
ADC is the standard abbreviation for aide-de-camp

explanation.surface: An officer's assistant slicing a map in a rash moment.
explanation.walkthrough: An aide-de-camp is an officer assisting a senior commander; 'up' only helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap scheme or person is wildly impulsive, so the adjective means rash.

clue.text: Sam gets hip broken in accident

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces that can be put back differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sam fractures a hip in a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky incident, a minor misfortune, close in meaning to an accident.

clue.text: Chess etc between top directors?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: games played on a board
second meaning, whimsically: contests within a company's board

explanation.surface: Executives playing chess against each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading, where the board is a company's directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess, draughts and the like are tabletop pastimes played on a marked surface.

clue.text: Fib about short name, which is the rule

indicators.note: one word wrapped about another surrounds it

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Lying about an abbreviated name is customary.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside LIE, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule is a straight stroke drawn with a ruler, the same as a drawn line.

clue.text: The airplane is visible only half way

indicators.note: only part of a word being on view means some of its letters show inside it

parts.note: the back half of this word

explanation.surface: A plane seen only partly, perhaps through cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half way' reads as one phrase, but 'way' is the definition and 'half' goes with the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A lane is a narrow road or route, so it is a way in the sense of a path.

clue.text: Being drunk, give gem to daughter

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Tipsy, someone hands a jewel to their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoned is slang for heavily intoxicated, whether by drink or drugs.

clue.text: Someone starts preserving and checking

indicators.note: where a word starts is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
canning preserves food in tins

explanation.surface: Someone begins making preserves and inspecting them.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanning is looking over something closely or quickly, a synonym for checking.
